findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django queryset raises an error or is unsafe
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a user-controlled negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError (a 500). The comment claiming the ORM handles it is wrong. The cursor offset comes from the request cursor string, which Cursor.from_string parses with no sign check. The 'authorization' for this path is only a client-supplied query flag plus a role check, so the feature is an unvalidated attack surface that was never needed.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now lets negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: The change in BasePaginator.get_result uses the raw offset when cursor.is_prev. A crafted prev cursor with a negative offset on any paginator that uses BasePaginator (many endpoints) now reaches queryset slicing with a negative start and raises an AssertionError. Previously the slice used offset directly, and a negative offset failed the same way, but the comment claims this is a deliberate feature. The edit is not behavior-preserving in intent and adds no validation. The same pattern is duplicated in the new class, and `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the unclamped offset.

findings.title: Authorization check may fail or be too broad
findings.body: organization_context.member can be None (for example for superusers who are not members), which raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits for superusers, but a non-member with other access would crash. Gating a pagination mode on is_superuser or global access is also weak protection for the unsafe negative-offset path. Trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89 also exists.

findings.title: New paginator is mostly duplicated code and has no tests
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result nearly verbatim, and get_item_key and value_from_cursor duplicate Paginator. It adds no real optimization. No tests cover the new paginator, the negative offset path, or the endpoint flag. Also get_item_key uses math.floor on a datetime, since order_by is -datetime, which raises TypeError. The optimized path therefore breaks on the audit log endpoint it is wired to.
